codeReview.summary: The implementation adds 4 destroy methods on VulkanRenderer (destroy_mesh, destroy_material, destroy_texture, destroy_skeleton) in a clean separate module (destroy_api.rs). AssetRegistry gains remove_mesh/remove_material returning Option<T>, plus a pub(crate) remove_pipeline. BindlessTextureManager gains release_texture_slot with default slot protection. TextureManager gains is_default_texture for default protection. All safety guarantees (double-destroy, NONE/unowned handles, default textures) are correctly implemented, leveraging ResourceStorage::remove returning None for invalid/already-removed handles. The commit also includes an unrelated pre-existing working-tree change adding the outline module/state to mod.rs, which the worker acknowledged. 10 unit tests cover all VAL assertions at the logic level; GPU-level integration testing is appropriately deferred.

issues.description: destroy_mesh does not have an explicit NONE guard like destroy_texture does. It relies on ResourceStorage::remove returning None for out-of-bounds indices (u32::MAX). This is safe but inconsistent — destroy_texture explicitly checks handle.is_none() while destroy_mesh, destroy_material, and destroy_skeleton do not. The behavior is correct either way, but the inconsistency could confuse future maintainers.

destroy_material destroys the material_descriptor_layout but does not free the material_descriptor_set. Currently material_descriptor_set is always None in the codebase, so this is not a practical issue. However, if descriptor sets are later populated, they would leak. The comment in the code only mentions destroying the layout.

test_default_textures_preserved tests only that TextureHandle::new(i) for i in 0..5 returns is_some(). It cannot actually verify is_default_texture() without a GPU context. The test provides minimal value — it essentially tests that handle indices 0-4 are not u32::MAX.

test_destroy_texture only verifies NONE handle detection, not actual texture destruction logic (release of bindless slot, TextureManager::destroy). Full GPU testing is appropriately deferred but the test name suggests broader coverage than it provides.

The worker acknowledged this but could not separate them with git add -p on Windows. This is a workflow friction point — git interactive staging doesn't work in non-interactive shells.

sharedStateObservations.observation: material_descriptor_set on MaterialAsset is currently always None (never populated by the material compiler). The destroy_material code destroys material_descriptor_layout but not material_descriptor_set. When descriptor sets are later populated, destroy_material will need to also free them.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: katla_gfx/src/vulkan/material/compiler.rs:246 and :292 both set material_descriptor_set: None. katla_gfx/src/renderer/destroy_api.rs:23 only destroys layout.

The architecture.md correctly documents this. Integration testing is deferred to the scene-load-gpu-cleanup feature which uses 25-frame mode.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: test_destroy_texture (line 77) is a logic-only test. Handoff coverage note: 'GPU-integration tests require Vulkan context and are deferred to scene-load-gpu-cleanup feature.'

sharedStateObservations.observation: The destroy_api.rs module uses `use super::*` glob import which is consistent with other renderer submodules (material_api.rs, skeleton_api.rs, etc.) — no issue, just noting the convention is followed.

summary: The gpu-destroy-apis feature is well-implemented and passes review. All four destroy methods (mesh, material, texture, skeleton) are correctly implemented with proper safety guarantees. Double-destroy and NONE/unowned handle safety is ensured through ResourceStorage::remove returning None for invalid indices. Default textures are protected by both an explicit is_default_texture guard and bindless slot protection (slots 0-4). The API crosses the katla_gfx/katla_app boundary correctly as confirmed by the scene-load-gpu-cleanup feature using these APIs. All 10 unit tests pass and the full workspace test suite passes. Four non-blocking issues noted: inconsistent NONE guard pattern across destroy methods, missing descriptor set cleanup in destroy_material (currently unused), and two tests with weaker-than-name-suggests coverage. None are blocking.
